chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), said:

I asked him about a man who was reached by the month of Ramadan while he was sick, so he died before he recovered. He said: There is nothing upon him, but the one who recovers should make up for him, then if that one dies before making it up, he makes it up for the one who died.
ai.seo_question: What happens to the missed fasts of a person who dies in Ramadan while sick?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of *qada* (making up) for those who die before fulfilling their Ramadan obligations, establishing that the debt is transferred to a capable heir or representative rather than being waived. It further extends this liability recursively, ensuring the obligation persists until fully discharged, reflecting the Shia juristic view of fasting as a personal debt (*haqq*) that can be vicariously fulfilled. This ruling underscores the continuity of spiritual accountability in Shia jurisprudence even after death.
